classification.difficultyReason: Requires coordinating signed ordinate operations, exponential growth and decay, turning behaviour and opposite tails without a supplied component graph. These remain routine linked procedures in the taught context.

answer.worked:
Subtract the ordinates of $y=2^x$ from those of $y=x$ at the same $x$-value.

$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=0-2^0\\y(0)&=-1\\y\left(\tfrac12\right)&=\tfrac12-2^{1/2}\\y\left(\tfrac12\right)&=\tfrac12-\sqrt2\end{align*}$$

Other guide points are $(-2,-\tfrac94)$, $(-1,-\tfrac32)$, $(1,-1)$, $(2,-2)$ and $(3,-5)$. Join smoothly: the curve has a maximum just to the right of the $y$-axis and remains below the $x$-axis. As $x\to-\infty$, $2^x\to0$, so the curve approaches $y=x$ from below. As $x\to\infty$, $2^x$ dominates and the curve falls without bound.

answer.worked:
Add the ordinates of $y=x$ and $y=2^{-x}$ at the same $x$-value.

$$\begin{align*}y(0)&=0+2^0\\y(0)&=1\\y\left(-\tfrac12\right)&=-\tfrac12+2^{1/2}\\y\left(-\tfrac12\right)&=\sqrt2-\tfrac12\end{align*}$$

Other guide points are $(-3,5)$, $(-2,2)$, $(-1,1)$, $(1,\tfrac32)$ and $(2,\tfrac94)$. Join smoothly: the curve has a minimum just to the left of the $y$-axis and remains above the $x$-axis. As $x\to\infty$, $2^{-x}\to0$, so the curve approaches $y=x$ from above. As $x\to-\infty$, $2^{-x}$ dominates and the curve rises without bound.
